newsitem.title: INDIA: India to get $7 bln aid from foreign donors.
newsitem.headline: India to get $7 bln aid from foreign donors.

text.p: India will get $7.0 billion in external aid from various multilateral and bilateral agencies, a government statement said on Thursday.
The statement said the total aid was decided at a meeting of of the India Development Forum held in Tokyo on Thursday.

The meeting was chaired by Joseph Wood, World Bank's vice president, South Asia region. The meeting was also attended by Heinz Vergin, director, India Country Department, World Bank and Edward Lim, chief representative of the Bank in India.
Montek Singh Ahluwalia, the highest ranking civil servant in the finance ministry led the Indian delegation.
International donors praised India's ongoing economic reforms saying a strong economic performance was achieved last year despite political uncertainty.
Japan was the largest donor with Y135 billion with its representative saying Tokyo appreciated "India's efforts made over the past five years".
India embarked on an economic reform programme in 1991 and has since then invited foreign investments in several sectors of industry.
The agencies, however, urged India to reduce fiscal deficits of both central government and the states.
They also asked India to expand infrastructure sectors, improve reforms in agriculture and make efforts to minimise subsidies.
